newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki slides, in-house deals give record volume.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki slides, in-house deals give record volume.

text.p: Shares ended a tense session sharply lower on Wednesday, tracking nervous European markets and Wall Street. Volumes hit a new record thanks to a big in-house deal, but brokers said there was no panic.
The HEX index fell 2.32 percent to 2,434.25 with volume for the day at 1.67 billion markka, up from the previous record of 1.6 billion markka set on Sept 2, 1993.
In-house transfers by state-owned asset management company Sponda in forestry groups UPM-Kymmene and Enso were behind the surge in trade.
"Stock markets have this week been so nervous that they turned easily lower," one broker said. He saw scope for more losses in Helsinki and overseas after recent sharp gains.
Forestries reversed most of their gains from Tuesday. UPM fell 3.60 markka to 94.10, Enso R fell 1.00 to 37.00.
Nokia slipped 7.00 markka to 261.00 despite giving largely upbeat signals at a briefing to some 100 international analysts here, according to one broker.
She said Nokia was also hit by rumours from New York that U.S. computer maker IBM was due to release a profit-warning, interest rate worries and other nerves.
But small caps bucked the trend.
Engineering company Vaahto hit a new calendar year high of 130.00 markka, up 9.00, in relatively heavy volume around 0.6 million markka -- after it announced a bonus issue on Tuesday.
